headline: Nineteen amendments filed, eleven moved, zero adopted
teaser: Councilors filed 19 amendments to the Moda Center term sheet. Eleven reached a roll call on Aug 6 — and the same six councilors voted Nay on every single one. Four failed on 6–6 ties. The final vote comes Aug 12.
body:
The term sheet — $120M from the City toward a $573M renovation, plus roughly $275M in maintenance commitments over 20 years — reached council with 19 proposed amendments from five councilors. What they would have done is spelled out under each roll call below: rent for the Blazers, a naming-rights share, proof of private financing, a higher payment-in-lieu-of-taxes escalator, and more.

**What the official record shows.** Eleven amendments were moved on Aug 6 and every one failed. The Nay column was identical all eleven times: **Clark, Zimmerman, Smith, Pirtle-Guiney, Ryan, Dunphy**. Koyama Lane, Green, Avalos, and Kanal voted Aye all eleven times; Morillo missed that mark only on Novick's amendment. Novick was the swing — Nay on the five-vote amendments, Aye on his own and the four that died 6–6. Amendments needed 7 votes; Mayor Wilson, who may break ties, broke none. The other eight filed amendments (Avalos 2–5 and 9–12) were never moved — not voted down, simply never brought to the floor.

**What council members said.** Council President Dunphy — elected in 2024 with Working Families Party backing and counted by Rose City Reform among the council's six-member Progressive Caucus — announced that he and Pirtle-Guiney intended to vote down every amendment, favoring a clean continuation of negotiations (per [OPB](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/08/06/portland-oregon-moda-center-trail-blazers-basketball/)). The amendment sponsors saw it differently; see the quotes below.

**Who spoke, and who didn't.** Per the meeting's broadcast captions ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qM1xO2aDjHc)): across the roughly 75 minutes of amendment debate (2:00:00–3:13:00), Councilor Zimmerman's voice appears only in the eleven roll calls — eleven Nos, with no floor remarks on any amendment's merits. He was not silent that afternoon on other business: at 12:24 he raised a point of order asking whether the mayor should cast a tie-breaking vote after a motion to reorder the agenda failed 6–6, and at 27:28 he questioned staff at length on the No Turn on Red ordinance. On the Moda amendments themselves, the record shows votes without explanation.

**What's next:** the resolution returns **Aug 12, 2026, 9:30 a.m.** for final amendments and a final vote; passage needs 7 of 12. Dunphy has said he may bring a comprehensive amendment incorporating the four 6–6 proposals (per OPB).

quotes.speaker: morillo
quotes.text: I am literally begging you to take these amendments seriously moving forward.

quotes.speaker: avalos
quotes.text: I think the current term sheet is absolutely unacceptable… otherwise I think we are failing Portlanders.

quotes.speaker: kanal
quotes.text: If we're in the video game, we're not at the big boss yet. We haven't gotten to a point where we're negotiating with the Blazers. We are looking at what we're even able to ask for.

quotes.speaker: zimmerman
quotes.text: In this case, would the mayor not cast a vote here?
